items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: So they would let me sit in — Gene Parker, Jimmy Cook, then more, like I say Marcus Belgrave — so then you learn more and more tunes.

ctx.x: I wanted to follow up way back, and you talking about sitting in in some of the places in Detroit when you were fairly young. How did you prepare to be ready for those moments? Because getting asked to sit in and then you get onstage and, “Well how about ‘Nardis’.” “No I don’t know that one.” Was there a way to get ready for that or did they let you suggest a tune?

Well luckily there was a really cool jazz club in Toledo, Ohio called Rusty’s. Her name was Rusty Monroe, and she had this club for many, many, many years. And she cooked the food. And I think I remember once like as she got older and she was telling me about how long it took for her to actually start making money as an owner of a jazz club. Because it was a very popular place, a lot of musicians who came through town — Joe Henderson played there, you know, and all the Detroit musicians would come down because it…

me, as a kid — what did I know, nothing. You know so they were very inviting, very like hey what do you know? So it was like okay, so the next time I go I’m going to learn two more songs, then three. Then you start learning more songs. And then eventually then I started playing with his band you know. In fact last night I did something and I ended this song a certain way and Ron says, “It sounds like an Eddie Abrams ending.” You know? So it was kind of a cool thing, because he had a particular thing and then…
